title: Stock status labels with nested IF
summary: Label every line Out of stock, Low, OK or Overstock with nested IF and AND, then turn the label into an action.

blocks.text: The store managers do not want to read stock numbers. They want a label: Out of stock, Low, OK or Overstock. The label then drives the action: reorder, markdown or nothing.
Four possible answers need more than one IF. You will nest IF functions, use AND for the OK range, and use OR to group the labels that mean reorder.

items: Objective: build a four-way text label with nested IF and AND.
You pass the mission at 80% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: A nested IF puts a second IF in the false branch. Excel checks the tests in order and stops at the first TRUE one.
Out of stock if on hand is 0. Otherwise OK if between minimum and maximum. Otherwise Low if below the minimum. Anything left is Overstock.
Order matters. 0 is also below the minimum, so if the Low test came first, an empty shelf would show Low. Put the most specific test first.
Text results need double quotes, and the spelling must be the same everywhere. Out of stock and Out-of-stock are different labels.

Tip: AND(B2>=C2,B2<=D2) includes both limits. A line at exactly the minimum or exactly the maximum is OK. Use OR when any of several labels should trigger the same action: OR(E2="Out of stock",E2="Low").
Four questions on nested IF with text labels. Type numbers without commas, for example 2.

items: Nested IF puts one IF inside the false branch of another.
Excel stops at the first TRUE test, so put the special cases first.
AND(B2>=C2,B2<=D2) checks a range, limits included.
Spell text labels exactly the same everywhere they are used or compared.

blocks.text: You have finished the rounding and logic group. Next in the curriculum are the conditional totals: SUMIF and COUNTIF.

items.prompt: Why does =IF(B2=0,"Out of stock",IF(B2<C2,"Low", ...)) test B2=0 before B2<C2?

options.label: Zero is also below the minimum, so the Low test would catch it first and hide Out of stock
Excel calculates the first test faster
Excel checks the labels in alphabetical order
IF cannot start with a less-than test

items.prompt: Minimum 10 and maximum 40 for every line. Stock on hand: 0, 10, 45, 5, 40. How many lines are labelled OK by AND(B2>=C2,B2<=D2)?
On hand (B2) is 50, minimum (C2) is 10 and maximum (D2) is 50. What does =AND(B2>=C2,B2<=D2) return?
Stock on hand is 8, minimum 10 and maximum 50. Which label does =IF(B2=0,"Out of stock",IF(AND(B2>=C2,B2<=D2),"OK",IF(B2<C2,"Low","Overstock"))) show?
